events.title: Bauernmarkt am Karmelitermarkt
events.description: One of Vienna’s biggest farmers’ markets, across the canal from the old town in Leopoldstadt. Regional meat, sausage and seasonal fruit and vegetables.
events.why: A neighbourhood market where locals actually shop, with good cafés around the square.

events.title: Flohmarkt am Naschmarkt
events.description: Vienna’s big Saturday flea market at the far end of the Naschmarkt: antiques, old books and records, household odds and ends.
events.why: Come early for the best finds, then walk back through the food stalls of the Naschmarkt.

events.title: Biomarkt Freyung
events.description: A small organic market on a square in the old town: fruit and vegetables, bread, cheese, honey and wine, plus baskets and crafts.
events.why: An easy stop between sights in the first district, with things to eat on the spot.

events.title: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte
events.description: Ceramics, textiles, jewellery and fashion by the women designers of the Wiener Werkstätte, the Vienna design workshop of the early 1900s.
events.why: Shows the side of Viennese design that the famous male names usually overshadow.

events.title: Bernhard Leitner: SOUNDSPACESCULPTURE
events.description: Rooms where sound is the sculpture: speakers move tones around you so you feel the space as much as hear it. At the gold-domed Secession building.
events.why: Something you can only experience in person, in one of Vienna’s best-known buildings.

events.title: Erika Giovanna Klien: All Is Movement
events.description: Paintings and drawings by Erika Giovanna Klien, a Viennese artist of the 1920s who tried to paint speed, machines and movement.
events.why: A chance to discover a woman modernist most visitors to Vienna have never heard of.

events.title: Robert Aldrich retrospective
events.dateNote: What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? Nov 21 · The Dirty Dozen Nov 22 · Kiss Me Deadly Nov 28
events.description: Over a month of films by the Hollywood director of tough westerns, war films and thrillers, shown in the Film Museum’s small cinema inside the Albertina.
events.why: Classic Hollywood on the big screen, in English, for the price of a cinema ticket.

events.title: Wien Modern
events.dateNote: Closing concert Nov 30 at the Musikverein
events.description: A month of new and experimental music in concert halls, clubs and museums around the city. Expect anything from orchestras to sound installations.
events.why: If you’re curious what classical music sounds like today, this is the month to hear it in Vienna.

events.title: Vienna Art Week
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A week of tours, talks, open studios and exhibitions with about 70 museums, galleries and art schools across the city.
events.why: Doors open that usually stay shut, from artists’ studios to behind-the-scenes museum tours.

events.title: Christmas Market at Schönbrunn Palace
events.description: A Christmas market in the courtyard in front of the Habsburg summer palace, with crafts, mulled wine and food stalls.
events.why: One of the first big markets to open, with the palace lit up behind it.

events.title: KlezMORE Festival
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A festival of klezmer, the traditional music of Eastern European Jews, with concerts, readings and films.
events.why: A rare chance to hear this music live in a city whose Jewish culture shaped so much of its past.

events.title: Wir sind noch einmal davongekommen
events.language: In German, with a subtitle app on your phone (English not confirmed)
events.description: Thornton Wilder’s wild comedy about one ordinary family surviving the Ice Age, a flood and war, all in one evening.
events.why: A big, playful show at Vienna’s most famous theatre.

events.title: La Fille du régiment
events.language: Sung in French. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A comic opera about a girl raised by a regiment of soldiers. It’s short, funny and a gentle first opera.
events.why: An easy, cheerful night at the opera, even if you’ve never been before.

events.title: Lass uns die Welt vergessen – Volksoper 1938
events.description: A play with music about this very theatre in 1938, when the Nazis took over Austria and its Jewish artists were forced out.
events.why: Vienna’s history told in the building where it happened, with English subtitles.

events.title: Auslöschung. Ein Zerfall
events.language: In German. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A stage version of Thomas Bernhard’s last novel, a furious, funny monologue by a man settling accounts with his Austrian family and home.
events.why: A rare €8 ticket to Vienna’s grandest theatre, for one night only.

events.title: Chicago
events.language: In German with the songs in English, German and English subtitles
events.description: The Broadway musical about two murderesses who turn their trials into a show. A new production at Vienna’s home of operetta and musicals.
events.why: The songs stay in English, so it works even if you speak no German.

events.title: Arnulf Rainer
events.description: A retrospective of Arnulf Rainer, the Austrian painter famous for painting over photos and his own pictures with dark, furious brushstrokes.
events.why: A new show on one of Austria’s best-known living artists, opening at the Albertina.

events.title: Winter im MQ: Opening
events.titleEnglish: Winter at the MQ: opening night
events.language: Songs, mostly in English and German
events.description: The courtyard of the MuseumsQuartier, Vienna’s big museum complex, starts its winter season with free live music from local bands and a DJ.
events.why: A free night out where young Viennese actually go, between the city’s modern art museums.

events.title: Wiener Konzerthaus Backstage Tour in English
events.description: A guided tour behind the scenes of one of Vienna’s two great concert halls, from the stage to the rooms the public never sees.
events.why: A cheap, daytime look inside a famous building, in English.

events.title: Viennese Christmas Market at Rathausplatz
events.dateNote: Opens Nov 13 · Ice rink until Jan 6
events.description: Vienna’s biggest Christmas market, in front of the neo-Gothic City Hall, with a giant tree, lights in the park and an ice rink.
events.why: The classic Viennese Christmas scene. Go on a weekday evening to avoid the worst crowds.

events.title: Weihnachtsmarkt am Spittelberg
events.description: Stalls of crafts and food in the narrow lanes of an old Biedermeier quarter behind the museum district.
events.why: Where many Viennese go for their mulled wine, with more handmade gifts than the big squares.

events.title: Art Advent am Karlsplatz
events.description: A Christmas market of arts and crafts on the square in front of the domed Karlskirche church, with makers selling their own work.
events.why: More handmade gifts and fewer souvenir stalls than the big markets, a short walk from the opera.

events.title: Die Fledermaus
events.language: In German with German and English subtitles
events.description: Johann Strauss’s operetta about a masked ball, a prank and a lot of champagne. Waltzes all the way through.
events.why: The most Viennese night out there is, in the theatre that has played it for decades.

events.title: Friday Afternoon
events.titleEnglish: Friday afternoon with the Vienna Boys’ Choir
events.venueNote: the Boys’ Choir’s own concert hall in the Augarten
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A concert by the Vienna Boys’ Choir in their own hall: Haydn, Mozart, Schubert and Strauss alongside pop and folk songs from around the world.
events.why: The easiest way to hear the famous choir in a proper concert rather than at mass.

events.title: Vienna 1900: guided tour in English
events.description: A guided walk through the MAK’s rooms on Vienna around 1900: furniture, glass and design from the age of Klimt and Otto Wagner.
events.why: A quick, friendly way into the city’s most famous design era, with someone to answer questions.

events.title: Kunst & Design Markt
events.description: Small designers, artists and makers selling fashion, jewellery, homeware and chocolate in the halls of a working Viennese brewery.
events.why: Gifts made in Vienna, bought from the people who made them, a long way from the souvenir shops.

events.title: Sonntagsmesse in der Hofburgkapelle
events.titleEnglish: Sunday mass with the Vienna Boys’ Choir or Girls’ Choir
events.venueNote: the chapel in the old palace
events.dateNote: Girls’ Choir Nov 15, 29 · Boys’ Choir Nov 22
events.description: A real Sunday mass in the palace chapel, sung by the Vienna Boys’ Choir or the Vienna Girls’ Choir with musicians from the State Opera orchestra.
events.why: The way the Boys’ Choir has sung for centuries, in the chapel it was founded for.

events.title: Madama Butterfly
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s heartbreaking opera about a young Japanese woman who waits years for the American officer who left her.
events.why: One of the most moving operas there is, with music many people already know.

events.title: Mnozil Brass: Strau$$. Ein Tänzchen zwischen den Stühlen
events.titleEnglish: Mnozil Brass: Strau$$. A Little Dance Between the Chairs
events.description: An Austrian brass band known for comic stage shows. This one takes on the music of Johann Strauss.
events.why: Viennese waltz music with a sense of humour, played by locals who know it inside out.

events.title: David Murray Quartet
events.description: The American saxophonist David Murray, one of the big voices of jazz since the 1970s, with his quartet.
events.why: A jazz legend up close in Vienna’s best jazz club, a small room where you sit a few metres from the stage.

events.title: Royal Concertgebouworkest / Klaus Mäkelä
events.dateNote: Also Nov 20, with Dvořák and Bartók
events.description: Amsterdam’s great orchestra, one of the best in the world, plays a Mahler symphony in Vienna’s golden concert hall.
events.why: A top touring orchestra in the hall many musicians call the best-sounding in the world.

events.title: Luisa Miller
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Verdi’s opera about a village girl whose love for a nobleman’s son is crushed by their fathers and a scheming steward.
events.why: Less often staged than Verdi’s big hits, with the same sweeping tunes and a story that is easy to follow.

events.title: Ariadne auf Naxos
events.language: Sung in German. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Richard Strauss’s opera about a rich man’s party where a tragic opera and a comedy troupe are told to perform at the same time.
events.why: The opera house’s big new production this month, opening while you’re here.

events.title: László Krasznahorkai: Im Wahn der Anderen
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: An evening with László Krasznahorkai, the Hungarian novelist who won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature.
events.why: A chance to hear a Nobel Prize–winning writer in person, in an intimate hall.

events.title: Kollegium Kalksburg / Agnes Palmisano Quartett: Alter vor Schönheit
events.titleEnglish: Kollegium Kalksburg / Agnes Palmisano Quartet: Age Before Beauty
events.description: Two groups who keep the Wienerlied (Viennese song) alive: a gruff, funny trio and a singer known for the Viennese yodel.
events.why: The city’s own folk music, played for locals rather than tourists.

events.title: Die letzten Tage der Menschheit
events.language: In German, with a subtitle app on your phone (English not confirmed)
events.description: A huge, bitter satire about the First World War by the Viennese writer Karl Kraus, built from real newspaper lines and overheard talk.
events.why: Vienna’s great anti-war play, staged by the city’s leading theatre.

events.title: Wiener Philharmoniker / Altinoglu / Buchbinder
events.description: The Vienna Philharmonic plays Gershwin, Ravel and Dutilleux in its home hall, with the much-loved Viennese pianist Rudolf Buchbinder.
events.why: The city’s own famous orchestra at home, playing some of its most approachable music.

events.title: Onegin
events.description: A ballet of Pushkin’s story: a bored young man rejects a girl’s love letter, then falls for her years later when it is too late.
events.why: One of the great story ballets, with a famous final duet, and easy to follow with no words at all.

events.title: Anna Netrebko: Bartók, Herzog Blaubarts Burg
events.language: Sung in Hungarian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Bartók’s short, dark opera about a bride who opens the seven locked doors of her husband’s castle. Anna Netrebko, one of the world’s best-known sopranos, sings.
events.why: A star soprano in an hour of intense music, in one of Vienna’s two great concert halls.

events.title: Lotte Reiniger: Die Abenteuer des Prinzen Achmed
events.language: Silent film with live music. Intertitle language not confirmed
events.description: The oldest surviving animated feature film, made in 1926 entirely from cut-paper silhouettes, shown with live music by two Viennese musicians.
events.why: A silent-film classic on a big screen with a live soundtrack, in a grand concert hall.

events.title: Ruin and Rush: Berlin 1910–1930
events.description: Painting and art from Berlin between the First World War and the end of the 1920s, when the city was broke, wild and full of new ideas.
events.why: The Berlin of Babylon Berlin and Cabaret, seen through the artists who lived it.

events.title: The Opposite of Now: Artistic Paths to a Different Present
events.dateNote: Last chance! Closes on Nov 22 · Closed Mondays and Sat Nov 14
events.description: A group show of contemporary art imagining other ways the present could look, inside Daniel Libeskind’s zigzag museum building.
events.why: Last weeks of the show, and the building itself is worth the trip.

events.title: Helmut Newton’s One-off Album
events.description: A one-of-a-kind photo album by Helmut Newton, the Berlin-born fashion photographer known for bold black-and-white pictures of women.
events.why: Last chance, in the photography museum by Zoo station that is also home to his foundation.

events.title: Gabriele Stötzer: Dabei sein und nicht schweigen
events.titleEnglish: Gabriele Stötzer: Showing Up and Not Remaining Silent
events.dateNote: Last chance! Closes on Dec 6 · Closed Tuesdays
events.description: The largest show yet for Gabriele Stötzer, an East German artist who has used her own body in photos, film and performance for five decades to push back against power.
events.why: Its last weeks, and a side of East German art you rarely see, next door to the Schlingensief and Kreuzberg shows.

events.title: Maurizio Cattelan. NIGHT
events.description: An exhibition by the Italian artist famous for a solid gold toilet and a banana taped to a wall.
events.why: His jokes land even if contemporary art usually leaves you cold.

events.title: Kreuzberg: Kunst und Migration seit 1960
events.description: Art about the guest workers from Turkey, Greece and Italy who moved to Kreuzberg from the 1960s, and how they changed the district.
events.why: Explains the Kreuzberg you see today, in a museum on its edge. Walk out into the neighbourhood after.

events.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
events.venueNote: contemporary art museum in a former railway station
events.description: Sound and video installations by the late Japanese composer behind the music for The Last Emperor and Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence.
events.why: An exhibition you listen to as much as look at, in a beautiful old station hall.

events.title: Carrie Mae Weems: The Heart of the Matter
events.venueNote: photography centre in the Amerika Haus by Zoo station
events.description: Photographs by an American artist known for her Kitchen Table Series, quiet staged pictures about family, race and power.
events.why: Berlin’s leading photography venue, showing one of the most important living photographers.

events.title: Christoph Schlingensief: Es ist nicht mehr mein Problem, macht eure Scheiße alleine
events.titleEnglish: Christoph Schlingensief: It’s Not My Problem Anymore, Deal With Your Own Shit
events.description: The biggest show in over a decade on a German provocateur who worked across film, theatre, opera and political stunts until his death in 2010.
events.why: A way into the angry, funny side of German culture after reunification.

events.title: Portraits! Surprising Encounters from Botticelli to Lempicka
events.description: Six centuries of portraits, from Botticelli, Dürer and Rubens to 1920s painter Tamara de Lempicka, hung in unexpected pairs.
events.why: Old masters you know, hung in surprising pairs, in a gallery that is rarely crowded.

events.title: Genghis Khan and the World of the Mongols
events.description: A big new exhibition on Genghis Khan and the vast Mongol empire he founded in the 1200s.
events.why: Recently opened, and a good reason to see the new entrance building on Museum Island.

events.title: Josef Kaiser: Building for the GDR
events.description: The East German architect behind Karl-Marx-Allee’s Kino International cinema, Hotel Berolina and Restaurant Moskau, the modernist side of 1960s East Berlin.
events.why: See the show, then go and look at the real buildings, which still stand on Karl-Marx-Allee.

events.title: Lunchkonzerte in der Philharmonie
events.titleEnglish: Free lunchtime concerts at the Philharmonie
events.description: A free 40–50 minute concert in the foyer of the home of the Berlin Philharmonic, usually chamber music or piano played by orchestra members and young players. Standing only.
events.why: The cheapest way inside the famous yellow concert hall. Come at least 45 minutes early: once the foyer is full, nobody else gets in.

events.title: Kunstmarkt am Zeughaus
events.titleEnglish: Art and book market at the Zeughaus
events.venueNote: by the river opposite Museum Island
events.description: A weekend market of art, prints and second-hand books on the riverbank between the Schlossbrücke bridge and Museum Island.
events.why: A browse that fits neatly between museums, and locals rate it for old books.

events.title: Street Food Thursday
events.description: Every Thursday evening a 19th-century market hall in Kreuzberg fills with food stalls from around the world, with beer from the hall’s own brewers.
events.why: A Berlin Thursday-night habit, busy with locals after work. Go hungry and early.

events.title: Wochenmarkt in der Markthalle Neun
events.description: The big market days at the Markthalle Neun: bakers, butchers, cheese makers and vegetable growers from around Berlin, plus cafés inside the hall.
events.why: Where Kreuzberg actually does its weekend shopping. Good for breakfast, bread and picnic food.

events.title: Flohmarkt im Mauerpark
events.description: Berlin’s best-known Sunday flea market, beside a park on the old Wall strip. Mostly private sellers with records, clothes, bikes, toys and furniture.
events.why: The classic Berlin Sunday: rummage, eat at the food stalls, then walk through the park where the Wall once ran.

events.title: INTERFILM 42
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Berlin’s short film festival, with screenings, talks and late-night programmes such as a long night of weird shorts.
events.why: Short films are an easy way to sample a lot of new cinema in one evening.

events.title: Interpol and Bloc Party
events.description: Two of the big indie rock bands of the early 2000s on one bill: New York’s Interpol, touring a new album, and London’s Bloc Party.
events.why: A night of the guitar bands that defined the 2000s, a short walk from the East Side Gallery.

events.title: NO LIMITS 2026
events.language: Varies by show, check each event
events.description: A festival of dance, theatre and performance by disabled artists from around the world, with opening night on Nov 11.
events.why: Work you won’t see elsewhere, with many shows designed so the language barrier barely matters.

events.title: West-Eastern Divan Orchestra + Daniel Barenboim
events.description: Daniel Barenboim, one of the world’s best-known conductors, leads the orchestra he founded with young Israeli and Arab musicians playing side by side.
events.why: A one-night chance to hear an orchestra that is as much a message of peace as a concert.

events.title: Berliner Philharmoniker: Zubin Mehta and Pinchas Zukerman with Bruch’s First Violin Concerto
events.dateNote: Two more dates, see event page
events.description: The Berlin Philharmonic plays Bruch’s warm, singing violin concerto and music by Dvořák with two veterans: conductor Zubin Mehta and violinist Pinchas Zukerman.
events.why: One of the world’s great orchestras, at home in its yellow concert hall, with two of classical music’s best-loved names.

events.title: Festival nowHERE
events.dateNote: Opening walk-through concert Nov 13 at 18:00 and 21:00 · Closing concert Nov 21 at 20:00
events.description: A week of new music at the Konzerthaus. It opens with a concert you walk through, across three halls, with 88 musicians spread among the audience.
events.why: The closing night pairs Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring with a live electronic set, a very Berlin mix.

events.title: Stereophonic
events.dateNote: Sold out, door tickets may be available
events.language: With English subtitles (spoken language not confirmed)
events.description: A play about a 1970s rock band recording an album while their relationships fall apart. It won Broadway’s top prize for a new play in 2024.
events.why: A hit play at one of Germany’s leading theatres, with English subtitles on this night.

events.title: 30 Years of Hamburger Bahnhof
events.dateNote: Open for 30 hours straight over the weekend
events.venueNote: contemporary art museum in a former railway station
events.language: Varies by event, check the programme
events.description: The city’s contemporary art museum turns 30 and stays open for 30 hours, with tours through the night, late performances, pyjama walks and film screenings.
events.why: Free entry all weekend, and a rare chance to walk an art museum in the middle of the night.

events.title: Ibrahim Maalouf & The Trumpets of Michel-Ange Vol. 2
events.description: A French-Lebanese trumpeter whose music mixes jazz with Arabic melodies, with his band.
events.why: A big-hearted, rhythmic concert in a classical hall, and easy to enjoy without knowing jazz.

events.title: La Calisto
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A 1650s Venetian opera in which the god Jupiter disguises himself to seduce a nymph, and his jealous wife takes revenge. Earthy, funny and sad by turns.
events.why: A new staging for the opera house’s baroque festival, played on period instruments, with seats from €10.

events.title: The Great Schlingensief Insult
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: An evening in memory of the provocateur Christoph Schlingensief, with friends including Nobel Prize-winning writer Elfriede Jelinek and Run Lola Run director Tom Tykwer.
events.why: Pairs well with the big Schlingensief show at the Gropius Bau, in the theatre where he made much of his work.

events.title: Reading List Berlin: No. 1 with Katie Kitamura
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: An evening of conversation with the American novelist Katie Kitamura, author of Intimacies and Audition, at the Volksbühne.
events.why: A chance to hear a much-read contemporary novelist in person in a small room.

events.title: Winter Market Schlossplatz
events.venueNote: in front of the Humboldt Forum
events.description: A new winter market with crafts, food and old fairground rides in front of the rebuilt Berlin palace in the historic centre.
events.why: Easy to combine with Museum Island across the water.

events.title: Madama Butterfly
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s opera about a young Japanese woman who waits years for the American naval officer who married her and left. A new production.
events.why: The first night of a new staging, with a party afterwards.

events.title: Christmas market at Charlottenburg Palace
events.description: A Christmas market in front of the lit-up baroque palace in the west of the city, with heated food tents and its own Christmas market orchestra.
events.why: The grandest backdrop of any Berlin Christmas market.

events.title: WeihnachtsZauber am Gendarmenmarkt
events.description: An upmarket Christmas market of white tents on one of Berlin’s grandest squares, between two domed churches and the concert hall.
events.why: The prettiest setting of any Berlin Christmas market, and quieter in its first days.

events.title: Alles Glück der Welt
events.titleEnglish: All the Happiness in the World
events.language: With English subtitles (spoken language not confirmed)
events.description: A new musical comedy based on a story by the East German writer Thomas Brasch, staged by his niece Lena Brasch.
events.why: A brand-new show at the city’s most rebellious playhouse, with English subtitles at every performance.

events.title: Die Blechtrommel
events.description: Günter Grass’s novel about a boy who refuses to grow up and drums his way through the Nazi years, staged at Brecht’s old theatre.
events.why: The 175th performance of a long-running hit, with English subtitles on this night.

events.title: Adventsmarkt am Kollwitzplatz
events.description: A small eco Christmas market on a leafy square in Prenzlauer Berg, held only on the four Sundays before Christmas.
events.why: A neighbourhood market where locals buy their Christmas presents, far calmer than the big ones in the centre.

events.title: RAW WINE
events.description: A one-day natural wine fair in the Markthalle Neun, with small winemakers pouring their own bottles.
events.why: An easy way to taste wine from many small producers in one afternoon, on a Sunday when the hall is usually shut.

events.title: La Bohème
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s opera about young, broke artists in Paris falling in and out of love. Big tunes, a sad ending, and a good first opera.
events.why: The classic first night at the opera, on the grand boulevard Unter den Linden, with seats from €11.

events.title: Ophelia’s Got Talent
events.description: A wild, mostly naked spectacle about water, women and drowning by Austrian choreographer Florentina Holzinger, with stunts and a huge water tank.
events.why: Holzinger is one of the most talked-about names in European theatre. Not for the squeamish.

events.title: The Hearing Trumpet
events.dateNote: Dec 3 premiere is sold out · Also Dec 6 at 18:00 and more dates in December
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A stage version of Leonora Carrington’s surreal novel about a 92-year-old woman who rebels against the care home she is sent to, made by filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger.
events.why: A free exhibition of Ottinger’s work fills the theatre’s gallery every afternoon too, 13:00–19:30.
